# Finding the Antiderivative of $-x^5 \sin(3x)$

## Setting Up Integration by Parts

I'll use repeated integration by parts (tabular method) on $\int x^5 \sin(3x)\, dx$, then negate the result.

**Tabular setup** (differentiate $x^5$ on the left, integrate $\sin(3x)$ on the right):

| Sign | Differentiate | Integrate |
|------|--------------|-----------|
| + | $x^5$ | $\sin(3x)$ |
| − | $5x^4$ | $-\frac{\cos(3x)}{3}$ |
| + | $20x^3$ | $-\frac{\sin(3x)}{9}$ |
| − | $60x^2$ | $\frac{\cos(3x)}{27}$ |
| + | $120x$ | $\frac{\sin(3x)}{81}$ |
| − | $120$ | $-\frac{\cos(3x)}{243}$ |

## Building the Result

$$\int x^5 \sin(3x)\,dx = -\frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3} + \frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9} + \frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27} - \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27} - \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81} + \frac{40\sin(3x)}{243}$$

## Negating for the Original Integral

$$\int -x^5 \sin(3x)\,dx = \frac{x^5\cos(3x)}{3} - \frac{5x^4\sin(3x)}{9} - \frac{20x^3\cos(3x)}{27} + \frac{20x^2\sin(3x)}{27} + \frac{40x\cos(3x)}{81} - \frac{40\sin(3x)}{243}$$

## Verification

Grouping as $F(x) = \cos(3x)\cdot P(x) + \sin(3x)\cdot Q(x)$ where:
- $P(x) = \frac{x^5}{3} - \frac{20x^3}{27} + \frac{40x}{81}$
- $Q(x) = -\frac{5x^4}{9} + \frac{20x^2}{27} - \frac{40}{243}$

Then $F'(x) = \cos(3x)[P'(x)+3Q(x)] + \sin(3x)[Q'(x)-3P(x)]$

- $P'(x) + 3Q(x) = 0$ ✓  
- $Q'(x) - 3P(x) = -x^5$ ✓  

Therefore $F'(x) = -x^5\sin(3x)$ ✓
